hood_landmark.Old Town (Medieval City): Palace of the Grand Master Rhodes Old Town

avoid.reason: Faliraki's bar strip is rowdy in peak season, and crowded Old Town lanes and beaches invite pickpocketing and tourist-menu overcharging.

hood_desc: Rhodes Old Town (Medieval City) is a UNESCO-listed maze of cobbled lanes, honey-colored stone walls and the Palace of the Grand Master, buzzing with tavernas and history. It suits travelers who want to sleep inside a living monument and do not mind noise, crowds and no car access.

Neochori (New Town) is the modern hub north of the Old Town, packed with beaches, bars, shops, the aquarium and casino. It suits first-timers and nightlife-seekers who want walkable amenities and seafront hotels close to the ferry port.

Ixia is a resort strip along the windier west coast just outside the city, lined with large hotels and windsurf-friendly pebble beaches. It suits couples and package tourists wanting spa resorts, sunsets and a short taxi ride into town.

Ialysos is a laid-back coastal suburb and windsurfing spot a bit further west, with family resorts and easy airport access. It suits water-sports fans and families who prefer a quieter, more affordable base than the city center.

Lindos is a whitewashed clifftop village about 50 km south, crowned by an ancient acropolis above turquoise bays. It suits romantics and day-trippers chasing postcard views, though its steep car-free lanes and summer crowds can be demanding.

water.note: Safe in Rhodes Town; in smaller villages and resorts, bottled water is the safer choice.

transit.pay: Pay cash: buy tickets at the kiosks/ticket booths by the New Market (Mandraki) bus terminals or from the driver for a small surcharge; contactless bank cards are generally not accepted onboard. RODA town rides cost about EUR 1.20-2.60, KTEL to Faliraki about EUR 2.50 and to Lindos about EUR 5.50 (roughly USD 6.50). Bring small bills or coins.
transit.hours: RODA city buses run roughly 6:30am to 8:30pm; KTEL coastal routes (east side to Faliraki/Lindos) run from about 6:15am until 10pm-midnight in summer, with no night service.
transit.note: Rhodes has no metro or trains: locals and tourists use RODA buses around Rhodes Town, KTEL buses down the east and west coasts (Faliraki, Lindos, airport), plus taxis; a rental car or scooter is the practical choice for exploring the wider island.

transit.m: RODA public bus (airport to Rhodes Town, ~40 min)

landmarks: Palace of the Grand Master
This imposing medieval castle, built by the Knights Hospitaller, dominates the Old Town skyline with its fortified towers and mosaic-floored halls straight out of a fairy tale.
Street of the Knights (Ippoton)
A perfectly preserved cobblestone medieval lane lined with the ornate stone inns of the Knights' various nationalities, evoking the atmosphere of a 14th-century crusader city.
Rhodes Old Town Walls and Moat
Encircling the entire medieval city, these massive fortifications are among the best-preserved in Europe and offer atmospheric walks along their dry moat gardens.
Mandraki Harbour
The picturesque old harbor where legend places the Colossus of Rhodes astride the entrance, now guarded by bronze deer statues and windmills along the pier.
Acropolis of Rhodes (Monte Smith)
Perched on a hill above the city, this ancient site holds the ruins of a Temple of Apollo, stadium, and odeon with panoramic sunset views over the Aegean.
Kahal Shalom Synagogue
The oldest synagogue in Greece, tucked in the atmospheric Jewish Quarter, offering a poignant window into Rhodes's centuries-old Sephardic Jewish community.
Suleiman Mosque
A striking pink-domed Ottoman mosque marking the highest point of the Old Town, a reminder of the island's layered Byzantine, Crusader, and Ottoman history.
Archaeological Museum of Rhodes
Housed in the Knights' grand medieval hospital, this museum displays treasures including the famed Aphrodite of Rhodes statue.
Rhodes Aquarium (Hydrobiological Station)
A charming Italian-era building at the island's northern tip showcasing Mediterranean marine life, set beside dramatic rocky coastline views.
Elli Beach and New Town Waterfront
The lively promenade beyond the Old Town walls, blending sandy beaches, Italian colonial architecture, and views toward the Turkish coast.

train.note: Rhodes is an island with no railway. Get around by KTEL Rhodes regional buses or hire car; long-distance travel is by ferry or plane.

bus.note: No international buses (Rhodes is an island). Local and island-wide services are run by KTEL Rhodes (https://ktelrodou.gr/).

ferry.note: International ferries leave from Rhodes Town main port to the Turkish coast; bring your passport as this is an EU/non-EU border crossing. Marmaris runs year-round (daily in summer, roughly Tue/Fri in winter); Fethiye is mainly a summer (April-October) service. Domestic ferries to Piraeus (Athens) and the Dodecanese are run by Blue Star Ferries and Dodekanisos Seaways.
